title: Ashtpadi 16, salok: no form, no color
hookLine: roop na rekh na rang kichh: He has no form, no outline, no color (Sukhmani 16)

lines: TWO DAYS AGO: IN HIS COLOR.
cards: Which is it? Two days ago, the picture was dye: everything soaked in His color. Today the very next ashtpadi opens by saying He has no color at all.

Is God the dye that soaks every thread, or something with no color whatsoever? It can look like a contradiction. It's a pattern worth learning to spot, because Gurbani holds the two together on purpose.

teach.h: ROOP, REKH, RANG: FORM, LINE, COLOR.
teach.b: The salok, in paraphrase: He has no form, no outline, no color at all; God is beyond the three qualities. Nanak, He makes Himself understood to the one with whom He is pleased. Three nos to start.
Roop: form, shape, appearance. Rekh: a line, an outline, the edge you'd trace if you drew something. Rang: color.
If you've been on this path since the start of the year, these may sound familiar.
Jaap Sahib, Guru Gobind Singh's morning hymn, opened the same way: no mark, no sign, no color, no caste.
Its short chachari lines said aroop hain, You are formless, and its opening verse even uses the salok's three words, roop, rang and rekh.
So Guru Arjan and Guru Gobind Singh describe the One in the same breath of negatives.

teach.h: LIGHT HAS NO COLOR, AND IS ALL COLOR.
teach.b: Now the puzzle: how can God have no color and also be the color everything happens in? Take light. White light has no color of its own; you can't point to it in a rainbow.

And yet every color you see is that light, split and shining. Or water: no shape of its own, and it takes the shape of every glass. Having no color of your own is exactly what lets you be in every color.
Something with a fixed outline can only be in one place; something with no outline can be everywhere.
Gurdwaras keep no images of God. In this picture, that isn't because God is far from shapes. It's that no single shape could hold the One.
Over the next two days, the salok's other phrases: beyond the three qualities, and known by those He blesses.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib open the sixteenth ashtpadi with the salok roop na rekh na rang kichh, and gurdwaras keep no images of God, since no single form could contain the Formless.

o: a holy symbol painted on a wall
a ray of sunlight through a window
a line or outline, the edge of a shape

games.q: the salok of ashtpadi 16 — tap the pairs.
p: no mark, no sign, no color

s: saying God has no color contradicts saying all happens in His color
like white light: no color of its own, and in every color.
Jaap Sahib opens with the same kind of negatives as this salok
no mark, no sign, no color: Jaap Sahib even names roop, rang and rekh.
gurdwaras use images to show what God looks like
they keep none: no single shape could hold the One.

games.q: Sukhmani says everything happens in His color, then says He has no color. how can both be true?
o: one of them is a mistake.
having no color of your own lets you be in every color.
games.why: like white light or water: no color or shape of its own, and so present in all of them.

practice: Close your eyes and notice what's behind the lids: maybe a dim glow, drifting specks, a soft darkness, no shapes worth naming.
Don't try to make a picture; rest in the not-picture, and if an image of anything starts to form, let it fade. If you pray, you can hold the word Waheguru without picturing anything at all.

wordCard.voice: Rekh, a line, an outline. Roop na rekh na rang: no form, no outline, no color, and so able to be in every form and every color.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: rekh, a line or outline, the edge of a shape.

carryVoice: Your line: no form, no color. And so, the One can be in every color. See you tomorrow.
